papers.title: When Do Restricted Sumsets Cover a Finite Abelian Group?
papers.summary: For A subset of a finite abelian group G, Sigma_k(A) = sums of k DISTINCT elements of A. Odd |G|: if |A| > |G|/3 + 1 then Sigma_k(A) = G for all 4 <= k <= |A|-4 (sharp). General G with least prime divisor p of |G| (fixed odd p, |G| large): exact threshold |A| >= |G|/p + p - 1 forces covering for k >= 2p-2; for 3 <= k <= 2p-3 restricted and ordinary k-fold covering have the same asymptotic threshold. Stated application: G = E(F_q); sharpens the Li-Wan-Zhang half-scale conjecture on MDS elliptic codes to a 1/3-scale bound when |E(F_q)| is odd.
papers.relevance: This is literally the COVERAGE question the monodromy closure leaves free (brief s.2: 'coverage (which targets decompose at all)'): with factor base F of size B in prime-order E(F_q), every target decomposes as a sum of k distinct base points once B > r/3 + 1 (for prime r, p = r so the general threshold is r/r + r - 1 ~ r, i.e. the structured threshold is useless and only the odd-order 1/3 bound bites). It therefore proves that for the cryptographic regime B << r^(1/2) covering must FAIL for 'most' A in the worst case and that no worst-case covering theorem can help; the useful residue is the proof technique (Fourier/rectification on restricted sumsets) for predicting the uncovered set of a STRUCTURED base. Concrete use: compute exactly, for toy prime-order curves (r ~ 2^20), the fraction of targets with zero k-decompositions over a structured base vs a random base of equal size, and test whether the structured deficit matches the restricted-sumset heuristics (a falsifier for 'better base geometry raises coverage').
papers.suggested_route: ideas/coverage_restricted_sumsets: toy census of Sigma_k(F) for structured vs random F; pair with Zhang-Wan deep-hole classification (below).

papers.title: Critical Numbers for Restricted Sumsets: Rigidity and Collapse in Finite Abelian Groups
papers.summary: Classifies critical numbers (smallest |A| such that Sigma(A) = G for the restricted sumset) in finite abelian groups: even order has an index-2 barrier fixing it at |G|/2 + 1; odd order collapses to much lower density, governed by index-5 obstructions or the smallest prime divisor. Resolves a Han-Ren conjecture: for all sufficiently large q, if a set P of rational points of E/F_q generates an MDS code then |P| <= |E(F_q)|/2.
papers.relevance: Companion to 2610.14496. MDS-ness of the elliptic code on evaluation set P is equivalent (via Cheng's Lemma 3 below) to 'no k distinct points of P sum to the fixed divisor point'; the result says a base avoiding any k-decomposition of a given target cannot exceed half the group. Inverse reading for index calculus: a base of size <= |E|/2 can be chosen so that a given target has NO decomposition, i.e. decomposability of a target is a property that base choice can switch off - a quantitative version of the programme's 'variance of yield is free'. Use: derive the k-fold version (how small a base can kill all k-sums to a target) and compare with the hypergeometric double-count mean.
papers.suggested_route: same experiment family as 2610.14496.

papers.title: Uniform sum-product phenomenon for algebraic groups and Bremner's conjecture
papers.authors: Joseph Harrison, Akshat Mudgal, Harry Schmidt
papers.summary: Generalised sum-product phenomenon in 1-dimensional algebraic groups over C (G_a, G_m, elliptic curves): a uniform Bourgain-Chang-type estimate, resolution of Bremner's conjecture on arithmetic progressions in coordinates of elliptic-curve points, an Elekes-Szabo-type result for small-doubling sets improving Bays-Breuillard, quantitatively optimal power saving. Tools: Diophantine geometry (David-Philippon, Laurent, Evertse-Schmidt-Schlickewei) plus the weak Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa theorem over Z (Gowers-Green-Manners-Tao).
papers.relevance: Over C only; nothing mod p. The relevant statement for index calculus is the shape: 'x-coordinates of points of E in a set with small additive doubling cannot be numerous' - i.e. a factor base defined by an additive condition on x (interval, arithmetic progression, small-digit set) is additively rigid as a subset of E. In F_p the only handle on x is 'x as an integer mod p' (brief s.2 'no subfield' wall) and this paper's methods (heights, subspace theorem) do not reduce mod p; so it names the obstruction rather than a route. Use: cite as the characteristic-zero reason why interval bases carry no extra additive structure; look for a finite-field analogue via Kerr-Mello-Shparlinski-style local-global transfer (below).
papers.suggested_route: obstruction note for interval/digit bases; no experiment.

papers.title: Additive Rigidity for x-Coordinates of Rational Points on Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: E/Q of rank r >= 1: if the x-coordinates of a positive proportion rho of a set of rational points lie in a d-dimensional proper generalized arithmetic progression, the number of such points is <= A(E,d,rho)^r. Consequences under small sumset (Freiman) or large additive energy (Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers): points whose x-coordinates have large additive energy obey the same rank-exponential bound. Methods: extraction lemmas, gap principles, spherical-code bounds, group law. Follow-up arXiv:2603.24340 (2026-03-25, v4 2026-07-28) generalises to simple abelian varieties via uniform Mordell-Lang: E(X) << |X|^2 and |X+X| >> |X|^2 for finite X in the image of a finite-rank subgroup under a finite morphism to P^n.
papers.relevance: Characteristic zero; nothing mod p. For the programme it is the clean statement of the heights wall from the additive side: the x-coordinates of a lift to E(Q) are additively unstructured (minimal additive energy), so any lifting route (xedni, height-compressing lifts, lever 11) cannot hope that lifted base points share digit/progression structure that a sieve could exploit. Use: cite in obstruction ledger for LEAD-TRF-global-lift-small-height / LEAD-EXO-global-lift-height.
papers.suggested_route: obstruction citation only.

papers.title: An effective local-global principle for algebraic varieties and the sum product problem in finite fields
papers.authors: Bryce Kerr, Jorge Mello, Igor Shparlinski
papers.summary: Transfers counts of zeros of integer polynomial systems over C to their reductions modulo sufficiently large primes (effective local-global), applied to congruences with products and reciprocals of linear forms; progress on the Murphy-Petridis-Roche-Newton-Rudnev-Shkredov question on an extreme case of Erdos-Szemeredi in F_p; v3 adds a result for almost all primes.
papers.relevance: This is the only mechanism found that moves sum-product statements from characteristic zero (where 2603.06483 and 2510.03828 live) to F_p for large p. If the elliptic-curve sum-product of Harrison-Mudgal-Schmidt could be pushed through such a transfer, one would get: for a factor base of points whose x lies in a short interval, the set {x(P+Q)} has large size/small energy - i.e. a theorem that sums of base points are 'spread', quantifying why the x-functional filters of KN-OPEN-91d4f6 cannot have growing gain. Sign is negative for IC but it would convert a measured closure into a proved one.
papers.suggested_route: theory note; attempt to state the F_p elliptic sum-product that would follow and check it numerically at p ~ 2^20.

papers.title: Bilinear character sums and sum-product problems on elliptic curves (and 'On the sum-product problem on elliptic curves')
papers.venue: arXiv:0806.0640; Proc. Edinb. Math. Soc. 2010; Shparlinski FFA 2008
papers.summary: Elliptic analogue of sum-product: for sets A,B of residues and a point P on an ordinary E/F_q, one of {x(aP)+x(bP)} or {x(abP)} must be large; proved via bounds on bilinear additive character sums over points on E. This is the baseline all later 'sum-product on elliptic curves' work cites; no finite-field successor newer than this was found by six searches and the arXiv API.
papers.relevance: The programme's exhausted lead LEAD-EXO-dl-character-sum-pseudorandom used the same character-sum machinery to test for DL bias; the sum-product form was not used. The x-functional filter question (KN-OPEN-91d4f6) asks whether a function of x correlates with the group sum; Ahmadi-Shparlinski-type bilinear bounds give the generic answer 'no, up to q^(1/2) error', which is the quantitative ceiling on any such filter at base sizes > q^(1/2). Below q^(1/2) the bounds are vacuous, which is exactly the index-calculus regime - the gap is the lever.
papers.suggested_route: cite as ceiling for KN-OPEN-91d4f6; experiment: measure the single-bucket gain of x-functional filters at B ~ q^(1/3), q^(1/4) versus the character-sum prediction.

papers.title: On Wagner's k-Tree Algorithm Over Integers
papers.summary: Rigorous, asymptotically tight upper and lower bounds on the success probability and complexity of Wagner's k-tree for average-case k-SUM over integers of range m and over Z_m, for ANY list size, confirming Wagner's heuristic n = m^(1/(log k + 1)) (earlier rigorous results - Lyubashevsky 2005, Shallue 2008, Joux-Kippen-Loss 2024 - needed larger lists). Includes an algorithm computing provably correct bounds for concrete parameters.
papers.relevance: Sharpens the programme's Wagner wall. Z_m has no small QUOTIENT either when m is prime; the k-tree still works there because Z_m has an ORDER (intervals are approximately closed under addition: 'size' is sub-additive). So the correct statement of the wall is: Wagner needs a size function s with s(a+b) <= s(a)+s(b) visible in the representation, not a quotient. E(F_q) has neither quotient nor sub-additive size (heights identity in the brief). This reformulation unifies the Wagner wall with the heights wall and the 'no smoothness' wall as ONE obstruction: absence of a sub-additive size function on E(F_q). Any x-functional filter with growing gain would be a sub-additive size and hence contradict this; proving that no bounded-degree function of x is approximately sub-additive is a concrete theorem target.
papers.suggested_route: theory: prove/measure that no degree-<=d polynomial f(x) satisfies Pr[f(x(P+Q)) small | f(x(P)),f(x(Q)) small] > baseline by more than O(d/sqrt q); this would close KN-OPEN-91d4f6 for polynomial filters.

papers.title: On the Regularity of the Generalized Birthday Problem
papers.authors: Lili Tang, Yao Sun, Xiaorui Gong
papers.summary: Observes the k-list GBP has an implicit 'regularity' (block-wise structure, as in Esser-Santini regular syndrome decoding) and builds an ISD-based framework: worst-case beats 2^(n/2) when k/n > 0.188 (regular) or > 0.11 (non-regular); BJMM-style heuristics suggest beating birthday for any constant k/n > 0 at density one; disproves the average-to-worst-case k-XOR conjecture for non-constant k; regular vs non-regular single-list GBP differ by sqrt 2 in the exponent; abstract says the average-case results extend to k-SUM. Applications: incremental hash attack, Requihash PoW.
papers.relevance: The relation-collection stage of IC is a many-solution k-SUM over E(F_q) with k = m+1 small and lists of size B; the regime where this paper wins (k linear in n, XOR/linear structure, ISD) is the opposite corner. The transferable element is the view of 'regular' lists = a partitioned factor base (e.g. Frobenius orbits, or x-interval blocks) and the sqrt-2 exponent effect of regularity on single-list GBP, which the programme's n^4 K^4 / r sort-and-match rate does not account for. Needs linear structure to go beyond that, which E(F_q) lacks.
papers.suggested_route: accounting check only: does block-regular base partitioning change the matched sort-and-match constant? (expected: constant factor, 'engineering').

papers.title: Fine-Grained Cryptanalysis: Tight Conditional Bounds for Dense k-SUM and k-XOR
papers.authors: Itai Dinur, Nathan Keller, Ohad Klein
papers.summary: Under the average-case k-SUM conjecture (sparse instances need ~ r^(ceil(k/2))), dense k-SUM/k-XOR (many solutions) cannot be solved faster than Wagner's k-tree for k = 3,4,5, and for k > 5 in a restricted parameter range; proof via self-reduction from sparse to dense instances plus Fourier-analytic obfuscation.
papers.relevance: Supports (does not create) the programme's closure that relation collection at m+1 = 4 or 5 summands cannot beat k-tree rates; since E(F_q) does not even admit k-tree, the generic rate stays at birthday. Value: a citable conditional LOWER bound for the k-list stage that complements the Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan preprocessing bound; together they say the only door is representation-dependence, consistent with brief s.2.
papers.suggested_route: citation in obstruction ledger; no experiment.

papers.title: Finding a Shortest Vector and More in 2^(n/2+o(n)) Time using q-ary Coset Difference Tree
papers.summary: Randomized exact SVP in 2^(n/2+o(n)) time and space (and CVP for dist <= 1.039 lambda_1 on Haar-Siegel random instances) via a q-ary analogue of the midpoint Hessian: the gradient of the periodic Gaussian at v/q is nearly proportional to a shortest vector v even after aggregating over a large random affine coset; the coset gradient is computed along a chain of intermediate lattices by a Wagner-generalized-birthday-inspired procedure.
papers.relevance: A fresh example of Wagner-style merging where the filter is a coset structure (L/qL) rather than low bits, and the aggregated statistic (a Gaussian gradient) survives summation - i.e. a 'sum-compatible filter' in the sense of LEAD-EXO-four-list-ktree-join. For E(F_q) the only coset structure is E/E[q]-style torsion, available only after lifting (p-adic/jet oracles, which are GGM-simulable per KN-FIND-002). So this does not open a door, but it is the current state of the art on what a sum-compatible filter can look like, and the Gaussian-gradient trick is new relative to the programme's filter inventory.
papers.suggested_route: idea seed only; any use needs a non-GGM-simulable coset, which brief s.2 says does not exist from group elements alone.

papers.title: The Approximate k-List Problem
papers.sublane: 2 k-list / generalized birthday (pre-window anchor named by the lane)
papers.summary: k-list problem where the k vectors need only sum to a target of SMALL HAMMING WEIGHT; algorithms for k = 2^m plus an approximate 3-list algorithm with better exponent than the 2-list case; trades list size (memory) against allowed weight.
papers.relevance: Approximate matching presupposes a metric on the group compatible with addition (Hamming weight on F_2^n). On E(F_q) the only candidate metrics are on coordinates (Hamming weight of x in F_{2^n}, |x| as integer mod p) and the heights/no-subfield walls say they are not sum-compatible beyond one bit. The programme's Hamming-ball bases (KN-OPEN-5e3dd0) and low-Hamming-weight DLP leads (LEAD-RHO-lhw-*) are the places where an approximate-k-list layer could be priced; no evidence it changes an exponent.
papers.suggested_route: none beyond pricing inside LEAD-ICB-nonlinear-frob-stable-bases.

papers.title: Hard Problems of Algebraic Geometry Codes
papers.sublane: 3 coding theory (the classical link named by the lane; read in full)
papers.summary: VERIFIED from the PDF. Setup: E/F_p with a point G of prime order q, evaluation points P_1..P_n in <G>, code C = ev_{P_i}(L((k-1)O)) (an elliptic one-point code of dimension k-1), received word R = ev(f') with f' in L(Q+(k-1)O) minus L((k-1)O). Lemma 3: dist(R,C) is n-k or n-k+1, and dist(R,C) = n-k IFF there exist k distinct evaluation points with P_{i1}+...+P_{ik} = Q (proof: f'-f has divisor sum P_ij - Q - (k-1)O). Theorem 1: minimum-distance of AG codes is NP-hard (randomized reduction from prime-field subset sum, codes from elliptic curves, alphabet p = O(q^2)). Theorem 2: a 2^(cn) (log q)^O(1) algorithm for minimum distance of these elliptic codes gives an ECDLP algorithm (splits the log into weight-n/2 pieces, Theorem 2 'for any constant c > 0'). Theorem 3: computing dist(R,C) for elliptic codes is NP-hard, hence ML decoding of AG codes NP-hard; Corollary 3 via preprocessing-subset-sum (Lobstein).
papers.relevance: Lemma 3 is an EXACT dictionary: the point decomposition problem 'is target Q a sum of k distinct factor-base points' equals bounded-distance decoding of the elliptic code on the factor base at radius n-k (one below covering radius n-k+1), and finding the decomposition equals finding the closest codeword. The programme has never phrased PDP this way (no hit for 'code', 'decod', 'Cheng' in atlas/treatise/frontier). Consequences: (a) every decoding algorithm for elliptic codes (Guruswami-Sudan list decoding, Beelen-Neiger, power decoding, Groebner/Welch-Berlekamp key-equation decoders) is a candidate PDP oracle whose cost can be priced; (b) the needed radius n-k is beyond list-decoding reach: with k = m+1 summands and base size n = B the code has dimension m and rate m/B; Guruswami-Sudan corrects up to n - sqrt(n(k-1)) = B - sqrt(Bm) errors, while a decomposition sits at B-(m+1) errors, so list decoding falls short by sqrt(Bm) - (m+1) errors (the Johnson-radius gap); (c) the theorem is about arbitrary evaluation sets; structured factor bases (subspaces, intervals) give structured codes, which is where coding theory may know more than Semaev systems do. This is the single strongest new connection in this lane.
papers.suggested_route: ideas/pdp_as_elliptic_code_decoding: (i) price GS/Beelen-Neiger list decoding of the length-B rate-(m)/B elliptic code at radius B-(m+1) vs Semaev solve at m=3,4, toy p ~ 2^20..2^30; (ii) ask whether the degree-m Semaev S_{m+1} equals (up to the x-projection) the key equation of a Welch-Berlekamp decoder for this code - if so the two formulations are the same object and the coding view adds nothing; if not, the decoder's algebra (rational interpolation on E) is a different presentation whose solving degree should be measured.

papers.title: Solving ECDLP via List Decoding
papers.summary: Builds elliptic codes from an ECDLP instance, gives an algorithm to find MINIMUM-WEIGHT codewords of AG (elliptic) codes via list decoding, and uses those codewords to solve ECDLP ('may provide a potential approach to speeding up'). The first author's 2019 CA/B Forum slides state the algorithm 'is not efficient currently, and it is even not of square-root time'. PDF not retrievable (403); construction and complexity UNVERIFIED here.
papers.relevance: The only prior attempt found to run Cheng's dictionary forward as an algorithm; the authors' own verdict (slower than sqrt) is consistent with the generic-oracle bound: a list decoder that only uses evaluation values at base points as abstract field elements is a generic algorithm with advice. It confirms that the coding route must use representation (structured evaluation sets) to be more than relabelling. Should be read in full before any experiment to avoid repeating it.
papers.suggested_route: obtain PDF (library/ProvSec), extract the exact decoder and radius, place it on the S*T^2 line.

papers.title: On Deep Holes of Elliptic Curve Codes
papers.date: 2022-07-26 (arXiv); IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory (year not confirmed)
papers.summary: Constructs deep holes (received words at covering radius) of elliptic curve codes and conjectures (analogue of Cheng-Murray for RS codes) that for long codes the construction is complete, with evidence from finite geometry; applies to curves with |E(F_q)| >= q+4. By Cheng's Lemma 3, a word ev(f') with f' in L(Q+(k-1)O) is a deep hole exactly when Q has NO representation as a sum of k distinct evaluation points.
papers.relevance: Deep-hole classification = classification of UNDECOMPOSABLE targets over the factor base, i.e. the complement of coverage. The conjectured completeness says that for long codes (B large relative to k, the IC regime) the only undecomposable targets are the 'obvious' ones from the construction; if true for structured bases it would mean coverage failures have an algebraic description and could be pre-screened (choose targets that decompose, cf. LEAD-ICP-coincidence-harvest 'escaping conservation by target preselection'). Also gives the Li-Wan-Zhang subset-sum counting literature as the right tool for exact decomposition counts over the full group.
papers.suggested_route: toy test: for a structured base F (subspace or interval) at p ~ 2^20, list targets with zero k-decompositions and check whether they are explained by the Zhang-Wan construction.

papers.title: Counting Subset Sums of Finite Abelian Groups
papers.sublane: 3 coding theory / additive counting (pre-window anchor, read)
papers.summary: VERIFIED. For A = Z_{n1} x ... x Z_{ns}, N(k,b) = (1/n) sum_{r | (n,k)} (-1)^{k + k/r} C(n/r, k/r) Phi(r,b) with Phi an explicit character-sum factor (Theorem 1.1); explicitly notes the case A = E(F_q) 'is related to the minimal distance of extended elliptic codes'; remarks that N_D(k,b) is polynomial-time computable by dynamic programming when |D| = |A|^c.
papers.relevance: The exact distinct-k-sum count over the FULL group is the baseline that the programme's 'mean yield is a double count' (monodromy closure) reproduces heuristically; Li-Wan make it exact and show it depends only on gcd(n,k) data, i.e. for prime r it is (1/r) C(r,k) up to O(1): perfectly uniform. Everything interesting (variance, structured bases) is in the deviation of N_D from N_A when D is a sparse structured subset; this paper and its successors (Li-Wan on D = A minus small sets) give the Fourier framework for that deviation.
papers.suggested_route: use as the exact null in the coverage experiments above.

papers.title: Combinatorial t-Designs from Finite Abelian Groups and Their Applications to Elliptic Curve Codes
papers.authors: Hengfeng Liu, Chunming Tang, Cuiling Fan, Rong Luo
papers.summary: Asks when the family of all k-subsets of a finite abelian group summing to a fixed element forms a t-design; full characterisation for 1-designs in abelian p-groups and exponent-pq groups; relates (t-1)-designs to t-designs; connects t-designs supported by minimum-weight codewords of elliptic curve codes to subset-sum designs on E(F_q). Companion arXiv:2506.16793 builds near-MDS codes of length > q+1 from elliptic codes and subset sums.
papers.relevance: A 1-design property for 'k-subsets summing to b' is exactly 'every base point lies in the same number of decompositions of b' - uniformity of the relation graph's column degrees, which the programme's rank-accounting lead (LEAD-ICE-relation-graph-rank-large-prime) needs. For the full group this is automatic; the question for a structured sub-base is whether design-like regularity persists, which would make relation-matrix rank predictable (ties to sub-lane 7).
papers.suggested_route: small: compute column-degree variance of the decomposition hypergraph for structured vs random bases; a design-like base would have zero variance.

papers.title: Dual and Covering Radii of Extended Algebraic Geometry Codes
papers.summary: Duals and minimum distances of extended and Roth-Lempel-type AG codes; covering radius of an [n,k] extended AG code takes one of g+2 values; for genus 1 it is one of two values when n is large or an [n,k+1] MDS elliptic code exists; g-MDS codes of length q+1+2g sqrt q from maximal curves.
papers.relevance: Minor: confirms the two-valued covering radius dichotomy (n-k vs n-k+1) that underlies Cheng's Lemma 3 for long elliptic codes, i.e. for long codes every target is either decomposable or a deep hole with no intermediate case; useful bookkeeping for the coverage census.
papers.suggested_route: citation.

papers.title: NP-Hardness of Bounded Distance Decoding for Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.summary: Extends NP-hardness of BDD for RS codes from additive gap O(log n / log log n) below the covering radius (Gandikota-Ghazi-Grigorescu) to polynomial gap d = floor(n^alpha), 0 < alpha < 1/2, via a prime-field completion theorem, an extension-field quotient construction and a deterministic condenser; hard instances have rate -> 1/2 and alphabet 2^(o(n)). Reduction from moments subset sum over nonzero field elements.
papers.relevance: Sits in the RS/F_q^* lineage where Cheng-Wan reduce finite-field DLP to RS decoding (and Augot-Morain run it forward to compute F_q^n logs). The elliptic lineage (Cheng 2005 above) has no comparable modern hardness or algorithmic follow-up; the new tools (prime-field completion, condensers over subset-sum instances in a group) are formulated for F_q^* and it is unclear whether they transfer to E(F_q) where no multiplicative/moment structure exists. Mainly a signpost that the F_q^* side is active in Sept 2026 while the elliptic side is dormant.
papers.suggested_route: none.

papers.title: Faster List Decoding of AG Codes
papers.summary: Faster Guruswami-Sudan-style list decoder for AG codes with improved operation counts (interpolation + root finding over the function field).
papers.relevance: The concrete tool to price Cheng's dictionary: list decoding of the length-B elliptic code reaches radius ~ B - sqrt(B(m)) but the decomposition radius is B-(m+1); the gap sqrt(Bm) - (m+1) errors is the obstruction (Johnson bound). Only a decoder beyond Johnson radius for the specific structured evaluation set would be a new oracle; for RS codes this is exactly the regime 2609.29120 shows is NP-hard in the worst case.
papers.suggested_route: pricing inside ideas/pdp_as_elliptic_code_decoding.

papers.title: A Sparse Overview on Sparse Resultants
papers.authors: Carles Checa, Ioannis Z. Emiris, Christos Konaxis
papers.sublane: 4 tropical / toric geometry of summation polynomials
papers.summary: Survey of theory and computation of sparse (toric) resultants: Canny-Emiris rational determinantal formula, Koszul-complex construction from n+1 nef divisors on a toric variety, computing the Newton polytope of the sparse resultant. No finite-field-specific content.
papers.relevance: The programme measured BKK/Newton-polytope sparsity as a 1.0-1.8x constant (treatise summer.tex DEC-20260806-26c0e8) and did not run sparse-resultant (Canny-Emiris) elimination, which builds a Macaulay-type matrix indexed by lattice points of a mixed subdivision rather than all monomials of degree <= D. For the Semaev system (S_{m+1} is degree 2^(m-1) in each variable with a highly symmetric support), the mixed-subdivision matrix is a candidate for a smaller presentation than the degree-D Macaulay matrix; whether it changes the solving degree (advance) or only the matrix size (engineering) is measurable. No literature applies it to summation polynomials (six searches).
papers.suggested_route: small experiment: compute the Newton polytope and mixed volume of the S_4/S_5 systems with one variable substituted (target), compare the Canny-Emiris matrix size against the Macaulay matrix at the measured solving degree, m = 3,4, toy p.

papers.title: Universal Analytic Groebner Bases and Tropical Geometry
papers.summary: Tate-algebra Groebner bases over valued fields; links the tropical variety of an ideal to its Tate completions; continues the tropical F5 line (Vaccon-Yokoyama 2017, Vaccon-Verron-Yokoyama ISSAC 2018 / JSC 2021) that makes Groebner computation valuation-aware over p-adics. No 2025-2026 successor found; nothing over F_p directly (tropical structure needs a valuation).
papers.relevance: Tropical Groebner bases need a nontrivial valuation; F_p has none, so the only way in is a p-adic lift of the Semaev system - and p-adic/jet oracles are GGM-simulable (KN-FIND-002, brief s.2). So tropical solving does not escape the generic bound unless the lift uses the integer representation of x (Coppersmith door), where the relevant literature is small-roots, not tropical. Negative result for this sub-lane, stated with its scope.
papers.suggested_route: none.

papers.title: Drinfeld modules may not be for isogeny based cryptography (talk title: 'Drinfeld Modules are not for Isogeny Based Cryptography')
papers.sublane: 5 Drinfeld modules / function-field analogies (brief s.3 lever 14)
papers.summary: Abstract: the Drinfeld-module discrete logarithm problem 'is easy even on a classical computer'; formulates Drinfeld analogues of SIDH/CSIDH and breaks them in classical polynomial time (isogeny computation by linear algebra; Wesolowski ePrint 2022/438 later gives the general polynomial-time isogeny algorithm). PDF 403; slides fetched contain only the isogeny part. MECHANISM AS I UNDERSTAND IT (unverified against the paper): for phi: F_q[T] -> K{tau}, the scalar action a -> phi_a is an F_q-LINEAR endomorphism of K (a sum of Frobenius powers), so phi(K) is a finite F_q[T]-module whose structure (Frobenius normal form of the matrix of phi_T on K = F_q^n) is linear algebra; the 'DLP' phi_a(P) = Q is then finding a polynomial in a known linear operator mapping one vector to another, i.e. linear algebra over F_q (annihilator / order computation), polynomial time. Leudiere-Scheidler 2026 (below) cite the DLP as 'readily computed' with reference [Sca01].
papers.relevance: Answers lever 14 ('what structural difference makes E(F_q) resist?') crisply: the Drinfeld group law and scalar action are F_q-linear in the ambient coordinates, so the whole problem lives inside linear algebra over F_q; the elliptic group law is a rational (nonlinear) map on coordinates, and the only linearity available is over Z (the group itself) or F_2 after Weil descent of the x-coordinate (where it costs the solving degree). The index-calculus analogy is therefore misleading: Drinfeld DLP is not 'index calculus works there', it is 'DLP is linear algebra there'. The honest transfer question is whether any F_q-linear shadow of E(F_q^n) exists (trace maps, Weil-descent coordinates) with nontrivial compatibility with the group law - which is the Weil descent programme itself. Closes lever 14 as a route; records the reason.
papers.suggested_route: theory note closing lever 14 with the F_q-linearity obstruction; verify mechanism from the PDF (library access) before filing.

papers.title: Public key cryptosystems based on Drinfeld modules are insecure
papers.id_or_url: J. Cryptology 14 (2001) 225-230 (bibliographic confirmation via CRAS 2003 note 10.1016/S1631-073X(03)00227-9 and IACR ePrint 2003/223)
papers.summary: The original insecurity result for Drinfeld-module public-key systems (the [Sca01] cited by Leudiere-Scheidler for 'discrete logarithms can be readily computed'). Content not read; title and venue confirmed from two citing sources. Blackburn-Cid-Galbraith (ePrint 2003/223) later recover the private key of the Gillard-Leprevost-Panchishkin-Roblot Drinfeld cryptosystem from the public key alone.
papers.relevance: Primary source for the Drinfeld DLP being easy; needed to pin the exact mechanism used in the obstruction note for lever 14.
papers.suggested_route: obtain and read.

papers.title: Computing submodules of points of general Drinfeld modules over finite fields
papers.summary: Algorithm for the structure of any submodule of the module of points of a Drinfeld A-module over a finite field (A a function ring over F_q), with Frobenius decomposition for A = F_q[T]; applies to isogeny kernels and torsion submodules; uses Frobenius normal forms, module presentations, Fitting ideals, linear algebra and fast Ore-polynomial arithmetic; SageMath implementation; complexity analysed. Related: Caruso-Leudiere arXiv:2307.02879 (characteristic polynomials of endomorphisms), Leudiere-Spaenlehauer arXiv:2203.06970 (group action from class field theory of imaginary hyperelliptic function fields).
papers.relevance: Shows the whole 'point group' of a Drinfeld module is computed as a module via normal forms of an F_q-linear operator - the structural statement behind the easy DLP. The elliptic analogue of 'Frobenius normal form of the scalar action' does not exist because [T] on E is not linear; this is the precise statement to put in the obstruction note.
papers.suggested_route: citation in lever-14 closure.

papers.title: A computational approach to Drinfeld modules
papers.authors: Cecile Armana, Elena Berardini, Xavier Caruso, Antoine Leudiere, Jade Nardi, Fabien Pazuki
papers.summary: Algorithmic survey of Drinfeld F_q[T]-modules of any rank: Carlitz module, arithmetic, analogies and differences with elliptic curves (rank structure, Anderson motives), SageMath code, applications to polynomial factorisation, isogeny computation, cryptographic constructions and coding theory.
papers.relevance: Entry point for the function-field side of lever 14; the 'differences with elliptic curves' section is the place to extract the exact list of structures (motive, F_q-linearity, Ore ring) absent for E(F_q).
papers.suggested_route: reading for the lever-14 note.

papers.title: A General Construction of Codes from Drinfeld Modules
papers.authors: Alessandro Giannoni, Giacomo Micheli, Mihran Papikian
papers.sublane: 5 Drinfeld modules x 3 coding (in past-few-weeks window)
papers.summary: Rank-metric and sum-rank-metric codes from bounded-degree morphisms between Drinfeld modules restricted to prime-to-characteristic torsion; supersingular case gives explicit dimension mrt - r(r-1)(d-1)/2 and distance r-t+1; characteristic-(T) case phi_T = tau^r gives an MSRD family identified with a skew-CRT code with polynomial-time unique decoding; Welch-Berlekamp-type filter equation in general.
papers.relevance: Illustrates again that in the Drinfeld world decoding is linear-algebraic (skew CRT, Welch-Berlekamp) because morphisms are F_q-linear. The elliptic-code analogue (Cheng) has no such linear decoder beyond Johnson radius - the same obstruction seen from the coding side. Tangential.
papers.suggested_route: none.

papers.title: Symmetric ideals, Specht polynomials and solutions to symmetric systems of equations
papers.authors: Philippe Moustrou, Cordian Riener, Hugues Verdure
papers.sublane: 6 representation / invariant theory of the summation-cover symmetry groups
papers.summary: For S_n-symmetric ideals I, relates leading monomials of elements of I to the Specht polynomials (of a given partition shape) contained in I; containing the Specht ideal of shape lambda forces the solution set into unions of 'few distinct coordinate values' loci and restricts the isotypic decomposition of R/I as an S_n-representation; gives information on the solutions of symmetric systems. Follow-ups found: Ishihara arXiv:2404.10482 (2024-04-16, primary decomposition of symmetric ideals via symmetry, Risa/Asir); Breloer-Riener arXiv:2606.18895 (2026-06-17, symmetric and isotypic Hilbert series for symmetric ideals, rationality); Debus-Gottwald arXiv:2506.15335 (2025-06-18, Specht ideals for type D and DIHEDRAL reflection groups).
papers.relevance: The Semaev system is S_{m+1}-symmetric (and (Z/2)^{m-1} x S_m after fixing the target). Decompositions into DISTINCT base points are the solutions off the 'two coordinates equal' Specht loci; a certificate that the degree-c truncation of the Semaev ideal contains the Specht polynomial of shape (m-1,1,1) would prove that all low-degree pseudo-solutions have a repeated coordinate - exactly the 'degree-c pseudo-solution' route the brief proposes for lever 1 (growth of the last fall degree), but organised by S_m-isotypic components so that each character block is a separate, smaller rank computation (lever 5, Frobenius/character-equivariant F4). Debus-Gottwald's dihedral Specht ideals are the right objects for the never-run D_4-symmetrised S_5 lattice (lever 3) and for the D_4 action on S_5 noted in the symmetry inventory. Nothing in the programme uses Specht/isotypic structure (grep: only Faugere-Svartz commutative-group blocks).
papers.suggested_route: ideas/isotypic_pseudosolutions: compute, at binary n = 13..21 and m = 3, the S_3-isotypic decomposition of the degree-<=c component of the descended Semaev ideal (msolve + hand-built projectors over F_2 need char != 2 for projectors - use the prime-field toy p ~ 2^20 with S_3 instead, or the sign/trivial split only), and test whether the sign component alone carries the last-fall-degree growth.

papers.title: Symmetric and Isotypic Hilbert Series for Symmetric Ideals
papers.summary: Defines symmetric and isotypic Hilbert series (per irreducible S_n-representation) for symmetric ideals, including in infinitely many variables, and proves rationality.
papers.relevance: An isotypic Hilbert series is a per-character count of the Macaulay matrix's rows/columns; for the S_m-symmetric Semaev system it predicts the block sizes of a character-equivariant F4 (lever 5) and gives a semi-regularity-style null hypothesis per block: a block whose actual rank falls below its isotypic Hilbert prediction is where the fall degree lives. Directly a tool for the 'first/last fall degree is a constant of the presentation' question.
papers.suggested_route: compute isotypic Hilbert series of the S_3/S_4 Semaev ideal truncations and compare with measured Macaulay ranks per block.

papers.title: Solving polynomial systems globally invariant under an action of the symmetric group (and SAGBI-Groebner for invariant systems)
papers.sublane: 6 invariant theory (pre-window anchor, already in programme)
papers.summary: Reduces an S_N-invariant system to systems in the invariant ring (elementary symmetric functions) cutting the solution count by >= N!; SAGBI-Groebner variant for general finite group invariants. Faugere-Gaudry-Huot-Renault (J. Cryptology 2014) and Faugere-Huot-Joux-Renault-Vitse (Eurocrypt 2014, symmetrized summation polynomials via 2-torsion) are the IC-specific applications.
papers.relevance: Already in the programme's symmetry inventory (Faugere-Svartz blocks 31-128x on rank; FGHR 30-416x on solve; D_4 on S_5 computed on paper, never run). Listed only to anchor novelty of the Specht/isotypic items above, which go beyond invariant-ring rewriting to the non-trivial isotypic components.
papers.suggested_route: none (run the D_4-symmetrised S_5 lattice, which the brief already lists as never run).

papers.title: The k-XORSAT threshold revisited (full-rank threshold of sparse random matrices over finite fields)
papers.authors: Amin Coja-Oghlan, Mihyun Kang, Lena Krieg, Maurice Rolvien
papers.venue: arXiv math.CO/math.PR; companion: Coja-Oghlan-Ergur-Gao-Hetterich-Rolvien 'The rank of sparse random matrices' (RSA 2022) and 'The full rank condition for sparse random matrices' (APPROX/RANDOM 2023, arXiv:2112.14090)
papers.sublane: 7 random matrix theory for sparse matrices over finite fields
papers.summary: Determines the full-row-rank threshold for sparse random m x n matrices over any finite field with exactly k nonzero entries per row (and, in the companion papers, the asymptotic rank for given row/column degree distributions), giving a simplified proof of the k-XORSAT threshold; rank deficiency is governed by a 2-core / matching-type fixed point (Lelarge's matching-number bound is tight in the binary case).
papers.relevance: The IC relation matrix is exactly a sparse random matrix over F_r (or F_2 after taking the kernel mod 2) with k = m+1 nonzeros per row and B columns; the number of relations needed for full COLUMN rank B is NOT B but is governed by the column-degree distribution (isolated/low-degree columns), i.e. the same fixed-point equations; the programme's relation-stage rank lead (LEAD-ICE-relation-graph-rank-large-prime, open_next_step) measures this empirically but has no theorem. The theorem also prices 'design-like' bases (sub-lane 3, 2506.00429): a base with uniform column degrees needs fewer excess relations than a random one by a computable constant. Constant-factor ('accounting') but exact.
papers.suggested_route: accounting: compare the measured excess-relation factor on the frontier ledgers with the Coja-Oghlan et al. fixed-point prediction for k = m+1.

papers.title: Probabilistic analysis on Macaulay matrices over finite fields and complexity of constructing Groebner bases
papers.sublane: 7 random matrix theory for Macaulay matrices
papers.summary: For random overdetermined systems of forms over any finite field, an upper bound on the degree of regularity holding with probability -> 1, depending only on numbers of variables, equations and degrees, via the rank of the degree-(d+D) Macaulay matrix; corollary (Tenti): quadratic semi-regular systems over F_2 with m >= n^2/6 equations have solving degree <= 3, so such systems are solvable in polynomial time w.h.p. Related: Bigdeli-De Negri-Dizdarevic-Gorla-Minko-Tsakou arXiv:2011.01032 (explicit solving-degree bounds for semi-regular systems, m > n).
papers.relevance: The programme's frontier row 'Modern Groebner-basis complexity refinements' probably covers this; it is the random-matrix theorem that justifies semi-regular null models for Boolean Macaulay matrices. The Semaev descent systems are NOT random (d_ff = 2 constant), so the theorem is the null the programme measures deviation from; the open question (growth of d_F) is precisely where the random-matrix prediction fails. Including for completeness of the lane.
papers.suggested_route: none beyond its current use as null.

papers.title: Smoothing the degree of regularity for polynomial systems
papers.authors: Samuel Jaques, Lars Ran, Simona Samardjiska, Melvin Seitner
papers.summary: XL/F4 cost is governed by an integer degree of regularity, which forces an unnecessarily overdetermined Macaulay matrix; the authors work at a 'fractional' degree using sub-matrices of the Macaulay matrix sufficient to solve, under an assumption generalising semi-regularity that they verify experimentally; smooths XL complexity for MQ and saves a few bits on a recent UOV attack.
papers.relevance: Directly a cost-model refinement for the decisive solving-degree cells (m,l) of the Weil-descended Semaev system: if the system is solvable from a sub-matrix between degrees d_F and d_F + 1, the cost table in docs/ic/CERTICOM131_IC_PROGRAM.md overstates by a fractional-degree factor. Engineering/accounting, but it touches the one quantity (D) the programme says is decisive.
papers.suggested_route: re-price the measured cells with fractional-degree Macaulay sub-matrices; check whether the generalised semi-regularity assumption even holds for descended Semaev systems (it probably fails, since d_ff = 2 is far below semi-regular).

papers.title: Probably correct row echelon form in the F4 algorithm
papers.summary: Gives the first bound on the failure probability of the Monagan-Pearce-Steel probabilistic row-echelon method used inside state-of-the-art F4 implementations, and a Las Vegas F4 variant that is correct always and faster than deterministic F4 on classical examples.
papers.relevance: Engineering: a certified probabilistic REF is relevant to the Frobenius-equivariant F4 on the full barrel system (lever 5) where the dense character blocks dominate; it does not touch exponents.
papers.suggested_route: engineering note for the F4 engine lead (LEAD-ICE-boolean-f4-f5-f6-engines is closed_dominated; only if lever 5 is revived).

lane_level_findings: Strongest new connection: Cheng (2005) Lemma 3 is an exact equivalence between the point decomposition problem over a factor base F and bounded-distance decoding of the elliptic one-point code on F at radius |F|-(m+1) (one below covering radius). The programme has no coding-theoretic formulation anywhere (grep-verified). The immediate obstruction is the Johnson radius: list decoding reaches |F| - sqrt(|F| m), short of |F|-(m+1) by ~ sqrt(|F| m); Zhang-Liu (2018/2019) tried to run it forward and report 'not even square-root time'. Any gain must come from the STRUCTURE of F (structured evaluation sets), which is also where the Semaev programme lives - so the key falsifier is whether the decoder's key equation is just the Semaev polynomial in disguise.

Coverage (left free by the monodromy closure) now has a literature: restricted-sumset covering thresholds (Han-Ren 2026-10-10; Chen-Huang 2026-02) prove covering only at |F| > |E|/3 or |E|/2, i.e. never in the IC regime, and deep-hole classification (Zhang-Wan 2022) conjectures an algebraic description of undecomposable targets for long codes. Li-Wan (2012) give the exact null count. A toy census of undecomposable targets for structured vs random bases is a clean falsifier for 'base geometry changes coverage'.

The Wagner wall should be restated: Lin-Vasudevan (2024) show k-tree works over Z_m (no quotient) because of a sub-additive size function (intervals). The real requirement is a sub-additive size, which unifies the Wagner, heights and no-smoothness walls into one: E(F_q) has no sub-additive size function visible in the representation. Proving that no bounded-degree polynomial in x is approximately sub-additive would close KN-OPEN-91d4f6 for polynomial filters.

Lever 14 (Drinfeld) closes as a route: the Drinfeld DLP is easy because the scalar action is F_q-LINEAR on the ambient field (module structure via Frobenius normal forms; Leudiere-Scheidler 2026, Joux-Narayanan 2019, Scanlon 2001), not because index calculus works there. The elliptic group law has no F_q-linear shadow except after Weil descent, where the price is the solving degree. Mechanism to be confirmed from the Joux-Narayanan / Scanlon PDFs (403 here).

Representation theory beyond invariant-ring rewriting is untouched by the programme: Specht ideals / isotypic decomposition (Moustrou-Riener-Verdure; Breloer-Riener 2026; Debus-Gottwald 2025 for dihedral groups) give per-character Macaulay rank predictions and a natural organisation of the 'degree-c pseudo-solution' proof route for last-fall-degree growth (lever 1) and for the never-run D_4-symmetrised S_5 (lever 3).

Tropical/toric: nothing in the literature applies Newton polytopes/mixed volumes/tropical solving to summation polynomials; the programme already measured BKK sparsity as 1.0-1.8x. Tropical Groebner needs a valuation (p-adic lift) and p-adic oracles are GGM-simulable. Only Canny-Emiris sparse-resultant matrices (vs degree-D Macaulay) remain unmeasured; expected 'engineering'.

Random-matrix theory: Coja-Oghlan et al. give exact full-rank thresholds for k-per-row sparse matrices over finite fields - the relation matrix - turning the open_next_step rank-accounting lead into a computable constant; Jaques-Ran-Samardjiska-Seitner (ASIACRYPT 2026, revised 2026-10-07) and Demin (2026-09-13) are in-window cost-model refinements for the solving stage. None changes an exponent.
